cards.front: What major danger did the original Sharpless-Meldal copper-catalyzed click chemistry present to living systems?
cards.back: Copper ions reacted with hydrogen peroxide to create toxic free radicals that destroyed living cells via the Fenton reaction.
cards.explanation: While great for test tubes, copper catalysts generated destructive free radicals that proved fatal to living cells.
options: It turned all treated cells completely magnetic.
Copper ions reacted with hydrogen peroxide to create toxic free radicals that destroyed living cells via the Fenton reaction.
It caused cells to instantly dissolve into pure water.
It permanently locked human DNA into a rigid spiral.

cards.episodeTitle: One Ångström at the Bioorthogonal Click
cards.front: How did Carolyn Bertozzi bypass the toxicity of copper in living organisms?
cards.back: By building spring-loaded, ring-shaped molecules that snap into place using stored geometric strain instead of metal catalysts.
cards.explanation: Ring-strained cyclooctynes store physical energy in their bent shapes, allowing them to react smoothly inside live tissue without needing toxic copper.
options: By using high-intensity X-rays to force chemical bonds.
By freezing the cells to absolute zero during the reaction.
By building spring-loaded, ring-shaped molecules that snap into place using stored geometric strain instead of metal catalysts.
By replacing all cellular water with heavy liquid nitrogen.
